collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 54 sovereign states that, according to Wikidata's currently-active driving-side claims (P1622 = Q11920728, left-hand traffic; with no end-time qualifier and not deprecated rank), use left-hand traffic, with their continent (P30) and most-recent recorded population (P1082). The row set is what the cited Wikidata snapshot reports for currently-active sovereign-state left-hand-traffic claims as of 2026-04-30; it is not a parametric reconstruction. Antarctica has no resident sovereign state and is excluded by construction; dependencies and territories with their own driving-side conventions (Hong Kong, Macau, Falkland Islands, Cayman Islands, etc.) are also excluded by the sovereignty filter and noted separately in open_questions.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (Wikidata SPARQL endpoint): universe + filter + value (defines the 54-row universe via P1622/P31; the WHERE predicate driving_side = left-hand traffic and the sovereignty filter together apply the set-filter primitive; supplies Continent via P30 and Population via P1082)

Single-source Tier A instance. The canonical SPARQL file at datasets/build_benchmark/sparql_queries/countries_drive_on_left.sparql is the universe-defining grounded artifact; running it via datasets/build_benchmark/sparql_to_csv.py with the documented rename map returns 57 raw bindings, which the documented post-processor collapses to 54 unique-Country rows (the three Pacific island states Kiribati, Solomon Islands, and Tuvalu carry both P30 = Oceania and P30 = Insular Oceania on Wikidata; Fiji carries only P30 = Insular Oceania). No separate validation source is used; cross-spot-check against Wikipedia's 'Left- and right-hand traffic' article matches the 54-row sovereign-state universe.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (Wikidata sovereign states with currently-active left-hand-traffic statements) is source-defined; ranking rule does not apply (set_filter has no inherent order, the CSV is alphabetized by Country); table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff because driving-side conventions are widely-known facts in pretraining corpora and most LLMs reliably recall the UK, Australia, Japan, India family of LHT countries; row count (54) is comfortably above the gate; confidence gradient is real (UK/Australia/Japan are very memorable, while Eswatini/Suriname/Tuvalu rank-membership exercises tail confidence).
- Seed/provenance: seed #2 from example_questions.txt ('Which countries drive on the left side of the road?'), verbatim with two columns added (Continent, Population) so the instance has the protocol-required 1+ key column AND 1+ numeric/categorical column.
- Category: set_filter (gap 3) primary; no secondary. The single-WHERE-predicate shape is the canonical set_filter primitive (driving_side = 'left').
- Source plan: Tier A Wikidata SPARQL; gt_construction = sparql_wikidata; source_count = 1.
- Expected shape: 54 rows x 3 columns; PK = Country.
- Domain: Transportation/Road Traffic — the **first instance in the Transportation family**, the largest family-level gap remaining (Law / Transportation / Environment / Education are unrepresented, per the 2026-04-30 picker snapshot).
- Risks/adaptation: Wikidata data quality required two non-trivial filters in the SPARQL: (1) the pq:P582 end-time qualifier filter to exclude historical claims (Argentina pre-1945, Sweden pre-Dagen-H 1967, Iceland pre-H-Day 1968, Czechoslovakia), and (2) the wdt:P31 wd:Q3624078 sovereign-state filter to exclude ~50+ noise entities (territories, dependencies, provinces, cities, individual people, roads, bridges, bus models, the European Union, etc.) that share a P1622 claim. Both filters are documented inside the SPARQL file as well.
- Decision: Stage.

SPARQL design: per references/sparql-gotchas.md §1, the universe-membership clause uses 'p:P1622/ps:P1622' rather than 'wdt:P1622' so that the rank-and-end-time filtering is explicit. A naive 'wdt:P1622 wd:Q11920728' returns 55 sovereign states including Argentina (whose pre-1945 left-hand-traffic and post-1945 right-hand-traffic statements are both at normal rank, so the truthy path returns both). With the end-time filter, the result drops to 54 currently-active LHT sovereign states.

Category <-> operation_type pairing: query_category=set_filter pairs canonically with operation_type=filter per references/artifact-contract.md. db_analog uses a single WHERE predicate (driving_side = 'left'). The Continent and Population columns are projection cells that come along for free; they do not change the structural primitive being tested.

Deviation from picker-guide order: the 2026-04-30 snapshot ranked seed #14 (G20) and seed #2 (drive on the left) both at ★★★★. Seed #2 was chosen for this slot to plant the Transportation family flag now (largest family-level gap) and because the SPARQL is trivial enough to ship cleanly Tier A; seed #14 will follow at the next slot.

Post-audit (2026-04-30): two non-blocking items addressed in this pass. (a) source_coverage_notes Roles wording was changed from 'universe + ranking + value' to 'universe + filter + value' because set_filter has no inherent ranking primitive — the role 'filter' more accurately reflects what Wikidata is doing (applying a WHERE predicate via the SPARQL FILTER clauses on P1622 and P31). The artifact-contract role table is described as a free-text convention rather than an enum, so 'filter' is acceptable as a free-text role label here. (b) draft.json::temporal_sensitivity was changed from 'low' to 'medium' because, although the row-set membership (which sovereign states drive on the left) is stable on a once-per-generation timescale, the Population column draws from Wikidata's most-recent P1082 statement and updates on a roughly annual cadence; the cities instance (top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent) sets the same precedent for Population-bearing tables. The semantic primary fact — driving-side membership — remains low-sensitivity; the change reflects the secondary Population attribute's drift.
normalization_decisions: Continent disambiguation: the three Pacific island states Kiribati, Solomon Islands, and Tuvalu carry both 'Oceania' (Q538) and 'Insular Oceania' (Q55643) values for their P30 (continent) property on Wikidata; the post-processor collapses both rows per country into a single canonical 'Oceania' label. Fiji carries only 'Insular Oceania' on Wikidata and is also normalized to 'Oceania' for cross-row consistency. No other countries in the result set have multi-continent P30 values. Country names follow Wikidata's English label verbatim, including 'The Bahamas' (with leading article), 'Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' (full official form), 'Timor-Leste' (Portuguese-form preferred over 'East Timor'), 'Eswatini' (post-2018 official form, not 'Swaziland'), 'Antigua and Barbuda', and 'Saint Kitts and Nevis'. Population is Wikidata's most-recent P1082 statement per country, taken as a plain integer; Wikidata's quantity precision and unit qualifiers are not preserved.
open_questions: 1. Whether the universe should be widened from sovereign states (54 rows) to include dependencies and territories that drive on the left (~22 additional entities: Hong Kong, Macau, all British Overseas Territories with permanent populations, Crown Dependencies, US Virgin Islands, external territories of Australia, Niue, Cook Islands, Tokelau, etc.). The Wikipedia 'Left- and right-hand traffic' article uses the broader interpretation (~76 total). Current v1 stays with sovereign states because the seed asks for 'countries' and most LLMs treat 'countries' colloquially as sovereign states. A v2 could broaden the universe and add a 'Type' column (sovereign_state / dependency / crown_dependency / etc.). 2. Whether the Population value should be anchored to a specific census year (currently uses Wikidata's most-recent P1082 statement, which can be 2020 for some countries and 2024 for others). The temporal_sensitivity is 'low' because the row membership is stable, but per-row Population precision varies. A v2 could add a 'Population reference year' column or pin to a single global year. 3. Whether the Continent value should follow the Wikidata-style 5-continent or 7-continent partition; current design uses the 6-continent variant (Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Oceania, South America) which Wikidata's P30 most often produces.
